speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To help me understand your specific situation, can you tell me exactly when this pain occurs and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the shooting pain triggered by chewing and pain from earrings suggests potential involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or a graft issue. Given your history of recurrent ear infections, have you noticed any drainage, discharge, or changes in hearing from your right ear since the surgery?
